paper.title: AUTOMATIC ARABIC SIGN LANGUAGE RECOGNITION: A REVIEW, TAXONOMY, OPEN CHALLENGES, RESEARCH ROADMAP AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS

description: A broad review of Arabic sign-language recognition covering alphabet, isolated-word and continuous recognition, with vision and wearable-sensor taxonomies.
reason: Meets M1–M3 as a broader review with qualifying CSLR coverage. Section 3.3.3 and Table 11 compare distinct vision-based continuous-sentence studies by methods, data and recognition performance.

M1.reason: Synthesizes prior Arabic SLR work in taxonomies and comparison tables.

M2.reason: Section3.3.3 and Table11 compare Tolba2013, Assaleh2010 and Assaleh2008 continuous recognition studies.

evidence.passage: Table11 compares Tolba2013 (PCNN/graph matching,30 sentences), Assaleh2010 (DCT/spatiotemporal HMM,40 sentences) and Assaleh2008 (DCT/HMM,40 sentences), including training/test information and recognition rates.

qualifying_studies: Tolba, Samir and Aboul-Ela (2013), Arabic sign language continuous sentences recognition using PCNN and graph matching [120]
Assaleh et al. (2010), Continuous Arabic Sign Language Recognition in User Dependent Mode [121]

assessments.reason: Retain for full-text assessment because review purpose and possible vision-based CSLR coverage are supported.
